author: Parshall, Jonathan
title: Research & Debate — Reflecting on Fuchida, or “A Tale of Three Whoppers”
publisher: Naval War College Review, vol. 63, no. 2 (Spring 2010), pp. 127–138
notes: The article that put the case against Fuchida's postwar testimony into a peer-reviewed journal, three of whose claims it takes apart one at a time — the first of them being that he had mentally earmarked the Pearl Harbor tank farms as targets. It is the reason this project cites Fuchida as a subject and not as an authority, and the companion to source:parshall-tully-2005. **The article's own PDF could not be opened from this environment**: the landing page above resolves, and the download returns 403, as history.army.mil does. What was read is Parshall's own restatement of the argument on his website (source:combinedfleet), which quotes the 1948 and 1963 interviews at issue; the citation chain is stated on the historiography card rather than hidden, in the manner docs/sources.md §7 asks for.
